title: As a Last Resort, Consider Exclusion to Reinvigorate a Wayward Team Member
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses the difficult problem of a team member who feels protected from consequences by bureaucracy, seniority, or a critical relationship and behaves defiantly as a result. It describes how appealing to such a person's good nature often backfires by emboldening further resistance, and proposes deliberate exclusion from meetings, updates, and team activities as an unconventional but sometimes effective intervention. The piece explains the psychological arc of this tactic, from initial relief at being excluded to eventual discomfort as social isolation sets in, framing it as a last resort before termination.
points: Some team members, protected by seniority, bureaucracy, or key relationships, come to believe they are immune from consequences.
Appealing to the good nature of a defiant team member can backfire, emboldening further resistance.
Deliberate exclusion from meetings and team activities is proposed as an unconventional last-resort intervention.
The excluded person's initial reaction is often relief or gloating before the isolation begins to wear on them.
This tactic is framed explicitly as a last resort before either tolerating the behavior or terminating the employee.
quotes: Team members sometimes act defiantly when they are protected by bureaucracy, a senior mentor, a critical client relationship, or deep institutional knowledge.
Unfortunately, appealing to the good nature of such a team member often empowers them to be even more resistant and hostile to playing along.
Perhaps nothing is more coercive to a team member than excluding them from the team.
As time goes on, the power of being a social being, first and foremost, sometimes takes precedence.
As a catalyst for resetting a rebellious and obstinate team member, exclusion offers a unique strategy that can sometimes work wonders.
